Job Description :
At EABL, we believe careers are built through meaningful experiences, and we take pride in continuously investing in future talent. We are committed to developing the next generation of professionals by providing students with opportunities to learn, contribute, and grow within a world-class organization.
This goes hand in hand with our ambition to create the best-performing, most trusted, and most respected consumer products company in Africa.
Our Undergraduate Internship Programme runs on a quarterly basis, with new intakes every three months.
If you are planning to undertake an internship between January 2027 and March 2027, we encourage you to apply now. Please ensure you indicate your preferred internship location when submitting your application.
What You Can Expect:
At EABL, interns are more than observers. We are looking for curious individuals who are ready to learn, ask questions, contribute ideas, and gain practical experience in a fast-paced environment.
During your internship, you will have the opportunity to:
+ Gain hands-on experience working on real business projects.
+ Learn from experienced professionals and leaders across the organisation.
+ Develop practical skills that complement your academic learning.
+ Build your professional network and workplace confidence.
To apply for the internship program:
+ Only students in their 3rd year or final year of study are eligible to apply. Applicants should intend to continue their education upon completion of the internship or be awaiting graduation. Candidates who completed their studies more than 12 months ago are unfortunately not eligible for this programme.
+ Be enrolled in a public or accredited private academic institution pursuing a Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification.
+ You must be on break/ holiday from school during the internship period.
Areas of Opportunity:
We offer internship opportunities to students pursuing studies in a wide range of subject areas, including but not limited to:
+ Business-related fields: Accounting, Finance, Economics, Actuarial Science, Business Administration, Marketing, Human Resources, Communication, Public Policy or Public Relations, Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Science and Analytics, Statistics, Project Management, and Supply Chain/Operations Management.
+ Manufacturing-related fields: Engineering (Chemical, Biochemical, Microbiology, Electrical, Industrial, Mechanical, Civil, or Packaging), Food Science and Technology, Environmental Science, Agriculture, Supply Chain Management, Procurement and Logistics, Quality Assurance, and Health, Safety & Environment.
Internship Opportunities Outside Nairobi:
Due to limited placement opportunities within Nairobi, we also offer internship placements within our subsidiaries and field-based teams across the country.
Applicants who are open to undertaking their internship outside Nairobi are encouraged to indicate this within their application, as this will assist us in matching them to available opportunities.
Current opportunities outside Nairobi include:
• Sales (Data Analysis & Insights) – Coast, Nyeri, Kisumu, and Nakuru
• Agriculture – Molo, Nakuru
• Food Science and Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, or Electrical) – Kisumu
• Information Technology / Computer Science – Kisumu
Indicating your flexibility to work in any of these locations will improve your likelihood of being matched to an available opportunity.
What you will need:
+ A successful intern has a desire to gain professional experience and is exceptionally eager to learn and explore possibilities.
+ Strong listening skills are also required to perform this role.
+ Oral and written communication skills, the ability to understand instructions, as well as not being afraid to ask questions will ensure a productive internship.
+ Excellent knowledge in use of Microsoft applications is needed.
+ Very articulate with fluent English.
+ Patient, attention to detail, fast learner, committed, able to understand directions, can work quickly and accurately under pressure.
+ Keen to learn about the markets and also with a high attention to detail and pride in their work at this initial stage of their career development.
+ A dedication to completing the 3 months internship program.
Mandatory Requirements:
+ Letter from your institution indicating you are a student there and/or require internship as part of requirement for course completion.
+ Personal Accident insurance cover for the duration of the internship.
+ Bank account details.
+ Copy of National Identity Card.
+ Copy of KRA Pin Certificate
+ NSSF and SHA numbers.
Critical Application Details:
+ When completing your application, please specify your current area of study or degree title under the Education or Work Experience sections. This information is required to help us match applicants to relevant departments. Failure to provide these details may affect your chances of selection.
+ The internship programme runs for a fixed period of three months and cannot be extended.
+ Applicants will be required to complete an online assessment once the application period closes in order to progress through the recruitment process.
+ We do not accept offline applications. Please refrain from delivering application documents to our offices. All applications must be submitted through the online application portal.
+ Please note that EABL does not charge any fees or request payment at any stage of the internship application or placement process. Be vigilant against fraudsters claiming to represent the company.

title: Business Support Coordinator – Internship
description:
KKCO East Africa LLP is a top-tier audit and accounting firm, recognized for its specialized advisory services that fuel business growth and strategic success. We combine financial precision with forward-thinking insights to deliver solutions that empower our clients to achieve their full potential and thrive in today's competitive landscape.  

**Reports to**  Administrator, with functional direction from the designated DFK Africa lead.  

**Location**  KKCO East Africa LLP  

# Role purpose  

Provide proactive coordination and business support, with primary responsibility for the DFK Africa office, its calendar of activities and sourcing prospective member firms across Africa. The role also supports KKCO’s document preparation, business development, administration and client experience.  

# Key responsibilities  

## DFK Africa coordination and membership development  

·       Coordinate day-to-day office activities, member communications, enquiries and records, ensuring timely responses and follow-through.  

·       Manage the annual activities calendar, including meetings, conferences, webinars and training; coordinate invitations, time zones, logistics, registration and reminders.  

·       Prepare agendas and meeting materials, record minutes, track agreed actions and follow up responsible persons.  

·       Identify and research prospective member firms across Africa; prepare firm profiles, undertake approved outreach and arrange introductory meetings.  

·       Maintain member and prospect databases and a recruitment pipeline; follow up applications, coordinate due diligence information and support onboarding.  

·       Coordinate referrals, introductions and joint initiatives; maintain activity budget and expense records and report progress, delays and decisions required.  

## Document preparation and administration  

·       Proofread, format and finalise reports, proposals, presentations and correspondence to KKCO’s professional and branding standards.  

·       Maintain templates, filing systems and action trackers; coordinate document review, approval, signature, printing, binding and circulation.  

·       Support the Administrator with office coordination and follow outstanding administrative actions through to completion.  

## KKCO business development support  

·       Capture enquiries and leads from all channels in the CRM; research prospects and prepare profiles and targeted prospect lists.  

·       Coordinate introductory meetings and proposal packs, credentials and capability statements; follow up proposals and agreed next steps.  

·       Maintain a weekly opportunity tracker showing ownership, status, next action and follow-up date; flag stalled opportunities.  

## Front office and client experience  

·       Welcome visitors, handle calls and enquiries, direct matters promptly and follow up unresolved issues; escalate sensitive matters.  

·       Coordinate meeting room bookings, readiness, refreshments and stationery; keep reception and client-facing spaces professional and welcoming.  

·       Keep signage and branded materials current; work with the Administrator and Marketing team to address presentation gaps and improve the client experience.  

# Accountability and priorities  

DFK Africa is the primary work priority. Agree a coordinated work plan with the DFK Africa lead and Administrator so that KKCO support duties are also delivered on time. Escalate competing deadlines early.  

The Coordinator owns coordination, presentation and follow-through. Technical teams retain responsibility for technical content; the Business Development lead retains responsibility for converting KKCO opportunities. DFK Africa leadership retains membership approvals, strategic decisions and authority to make commitments.  

# Performance measures  

·       DFK Africa calendar is current and activities are coordinated within agreed timelines.  

·       Meeting records and action trackers are accurate, with overdue matters followed up or escalated.  

·       Prospect sourcing, approved outreach and introductory meetings meet agreed targets; recruitment progress is reported monthly.  

·       Member records, applications and onboarding actions remain current and are followed through promptly.  

·       Documents meet agreed quality, branding and turnaround standards.  

·       KKCO leads and proposals have clear owners, next actions and follow-up dates; the opportunity tracker is updated weekly.  

·       Client enquiries are handled promptly and client-facing spaces are consistently ready and professional.  

# Core competencies  

Proactivity and ownership; reliable follow-through; strong organisation and attention to detail; clear writing, proofreading and research; professional client service; cross-cultural communication; curiosity, practical problem solving and digital confidence. Sound judgment, confidentiality and responsible use of AI are essential.  

  

  

### Requirements

# Qualifications and experience  

·       Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Communications, Management or a related field.  

·       Experience in professional services, membership recruitment, networks or multi-country coordination is an advantage.  

·       Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook; familiarity with CRM, task-management and AI productivity tools.  

  

**DEADLINE - 13th November 2026**

description:
About Us
Action Against Hunger USA is part of the Action Against Hunger International network, a global leader in the fight against hunger operating in over 50 countries with programs focused on nutrition, health, climate resilience, food security, emergency response, and resilience building. About the Role
The Data Management Intern will provide day-to-day support to Action Against Hunger’s data management, reporting, and digital information systems. Reporting to the Data Manager, this role will assist with data capture, data cleaning, data quality checks, dashboard updates, user support, documentation, and report preparation for MEAL and program teams.
This internship will provide practical exposure to DHIS2 operations, Excel/Google Sheets, mobile data collection tools, Power BI dashboards, and basic data interoperability workflows. This position is ideal for an early-career data, MEAL, public health, or information systems professional with strong attention to detail, a willingness to learn, and an interest in humanitarian data systems.
Key Responsibilities

Support routine data cleaning, validation, and preparation of datasets for MEAL and program reporting.
Assist with basic configuration updates in DHIS2 and other data systems, including data elements, indicators, datasets, forms, option sets, and user access settings.
Support routine data quality checks to identify missing values, duplicates, outliers, inconsistencies, and reporting gaps.
Assist with dashboard and report updates in DHIS2, Power BI, Excel, and Google Sheets.
Support routine data exports for monthly, quarterly, donor, and internal reporting processes.
Assist with testing DHIS2 forms, dashboards, reports, and digital tools before deployment or release to users.
Document bugs, user feedback, system issues, and follow-up actions in organized trackers.
Provide basic first-level user support, including login assistance, account setup support, how-to guidance, and simple troubleshooting.
Support the preparation and maintenance of user guides, quick-reference sheets, FAQs, training slides, standard operating procedures, and knowledge management materials.
Assist with training coordination, including attendance tracking, practical exercises, and participant follow-up.
Support basic data import, export, extraction, cleaning, and transformation processes using approved tools and guidance.
Participate in MEAL, data, and program meetings as required and contribute to continuous improvement of data tools, workflows, dashboards, and reporting templates.

Who We’re Looking For

Bachelor’s degree, diploma, or ongoing studies in Statistics, Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, Public Health, Monitoring and Evaluation, Project Management, or a related field.
Training or coursework in data management, database systems, monitoring and evaluation, analytics, or information systems is an added advantage.
Demonstrated interest in humanitarian programming, MEAL, digital data systems, or public health data management.
Basic knowledge of data collection, data entry, data cleaning, and data quality assurance principles.
Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including basic formulas, sorting, filtering, and data validation.
Familiarity with DHIS2, Power BI, Kobo/ODK, CommCare, mobile data collection tools, SQL, or scripting tools is an added advantage.
Strong attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies, missing data, duplicate records, and reporting gaps.
Ability to follow instructions, standard operating procedures, checklists, and testing scripts accurately.
Good documentation skills, including the ability to prepare user guides, trackers, meeting notes, and simple reports.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to support users patiently and professionally.
Ability to work in a dynamic environment, manage assigned tasks, meet deadlines, and ask for support when needed.
High level of confidentiality and commitment to responsible handling of program and beneficiary data.
Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of Kiswahili is an added advantage.
Commitment to Action Against Hunger’s values, gender equality commitments, and safeguarding principles.

Why Join Us?
Join Action Against Hunger to gain practical experience supporting humanitarian data systems, reporting processes, and digital information management in a dynamic international NGO environment.
In this internship, you will work closely with MEAL, program, and data management colleagues to support timely, accurate, and reliable information for decision-making across Kenya and the Nairobi hub. This is an opportunity to build hands-on experience with tools such as DHIS2, Excel/Google Sheets, mobile data collection platforms, and Power BI while contributing to programs that support communities affected by hunger, emergencies, and climate-related challenges.
